objective: Reduce measured compilation time/allocation of the general V8 dispatch/terminal-peeling candidate while preserving runtime gains.
method: Inspect saved phase statistics, collect native compiler samples, then choose a source change with a concrete invariant. No benchmark-specific runtime behavior.

protocol.isolation: Serial builds/tests/profiles/benchmarks; read-only analysis may overlap.
protocol.compilation_diagnostics: Six fixed alternating AB/BA pairs after one warmup per binary, unchanged official DataView suite with the same synchronous compiler-statistics flags as the prior experiment.
protocol.runtime_validation: Leading cost candidate: 21 fixed alternating AB/BA pairs on unchanged official DataView suite with stock flags.
protocol.official_compiler_validation: Leading cost candidate: 12 fixed alternating AB/BA pairs on unchanged official Compiler suite; all nine cases reported.
protocol.checkpoints: Unsigned source and result commits for every experiment, including rejected candidates.
protocol.acceptance: Report both cost and runtime changes, native code size, count differences, and confidence intervals. Fewer allocations alone are not evidence of faster compilation.
